messages:
maya: FYI — XCorp just asked for a weird mix: carry-over trial credits, per-route priority lanes, and a regional capacity guarantee for APAC. Sales says this is gating the contract.
sam: Ugh. Do they mean convert trial credits into reserved capacity, or just let unused credits roll over?
chris (sales): They want unused trial credits to apply toward the first-month reserved commit, plus ability to punch through priority lanes during spikes. Their legal also flagged data residency.
liam: Two separate concerns operationally: 1) carry-over credits => billing & metering changes; 2) per-route priority => routing/router queue isolation or QoS. Both have infra cost/complexity.
anya: I can run a quick simulation of uplift. If we allow conversion up to 30% of trial credits into the first-month commit, cost delta looks small for typical usage. But unlimited carryover is risky.
beth (legal): Need to see exact language. Carry-over + conversion into reserved commit has revenue recognition implications. Also must redact any SLA on capacity unless we include hard guardrails.
maya: Can we propose a bounded compromise to unblock sales? e.g., carry-over capped at 30%, 90-day window, and a per-route soft-priority (best-effort with credits) rather than hard SLA.
chris (sales): That would probably work for them as a stopgap. They asked specifically for per-route priority because they have a latency-sensitive checkout flow in APAC.
sam: Implementation-wise, soft-priority could be a tokens-based priority lane: when they hit X tokens/minute for a route, they consume priority credits which pull from a reserved burst pool. Easier than dedicated isolation.
liam: Agreed. That maps to existing burst pool model. We should add a per-route cap so noisy routes can't consume all priority.
anya: I sketched some numbers: if we cap carryover at 30% and priority-credit refill rate at 10k tokens/minute per customer, expected cost is ~+6% infra at peak for APAC. That’s acceptable with pricing adjustments.
beth (legal): Draft language suggestion: 
```
- Customer trial credits up to 30% may be applied to the first-month reserved commitment if exercised within 90 days of trial end.
- Priority lane usage is best-effort and consumes priority credits from Customer’s Burst Pool. Priority lane does not constitute a guarantee of dedicated capacity or latency SLA.
```
liam: That legal wording is good. Ops still needs explicit guardrails: region-level soft quota, fallback model (auto-failover to standard lane), and observability hooks.
ops-bot: /note Created ticket INF-4231 for priority-lane feature prototype and ticket BILL-2142 for billing flow change.
maya: Proposed go/no-go: Prototype priority-credit lane + billing conversion clause as optional add-on. Launch criteria: demo with ops, legal-approved contract language, and a sales pilot doc.
chris (sales): I'll push this to XCorp and ask if 30%/90-day is acceptable. If yes, we can close this week.
anya: I'll attach the cost model and a 3-scenario sensitivity (low/medium/high).
sam: Engineering rough effort: priority-lane prototype ~3 sprint points (1 sprint), billing conversion ~2 sprints to hook into invoices, plus e2e tests.
beth (legal): I'll draft an addendum; need product to confirm exact numeric caps before I finalize.
maya: Great. Action items: @anya model due EOD tomorrow, @liam ops spec draft by Tues, @beth addendum draft by Wed, @chris confirm customer acceptance. We'll reconvene Thurs if needed.
chris (sales): :thumbsup: will update.
liam: One more thing — add observability: per-route cost & latency scoreboard so we can trigger regression alerts if priority lanes increase p99 by >20%.
anya: noted. I'll add metric KPIs to the sensitivity doc.
maya: Thanks team. If XCorp signs this, we should bake this pattern into a new 'onramp credits' add-on in the roadmap — low-risk template for future deals.
chris (sales): Sounds good; I flagged it as a repeatable playbook in CRM.
maya: End thread.
